I’ve just finished a series of edits to the Glint agent’s core logic to better handle cases where the model’s reply ends up empty—i.e., all its intended tool calls get stuck in the reasoning channel. By adding the `emptyNudges` counter and the associated “stall guard” in `agent.ts`, the system can now nudge the model to produce a visible reply when it otherwise would stay silent. The edit succeeded, and the file now contains the new logic for detecting an empty reply, pushing a “continue” message, and incrementing `emptyNudges`.

Now that the code can detect and nudge empty replies, I need to make sure the model’s own prompting also discourages it from simply giving up when it encounters a failure or a dead‑end. The prompts that drive the model’s behavior live in `src/core/prompts.ts`. There’s already a line there that tells the model “Reporting failure honestly is always acceptable…”. That line is a good anchor point for adding more explicit guidance about persistence.

Looking at the current content of `prompts.ts`, I see the exact string:

```
- Reporting failure honestly is always acceptable. Claiming success that did not happen is the one unforgivable behavior — if your last run failed, the task is not done.
```

I want to extend this with an additional bullet that says the model should never stop midway and must keep diagnosing, fixing, and rerunning until the task is truly complete (or a hard blocker requiring user intervention appears). This will reinforce the new “empty reply” handling and align the model’s high‑level instructions with the low‑level guard I just added.

The edit operation I need is a simple replacement: locate the exact old string (the line above) and replace it with a new string that includes the original line plus a newline and the new bullet. I must be careful not to set `replace_all` to true; I only want to replace this single occurrence. The new string should be:

```
- Reporting failure honestly is always acceptable. Claiming success that did not happen is the one unforgivable behavior — if your last run failed, the task is not done.
- Never stop midway. Keep working — diagnose, fix, rerun — until the task is done or you hit a hard blocker only the user can resolve. Describing what should be done is not doing it.
```

By inserting this directly after the existing line, the prompt will now convey both honesty about failure and a firm rule against premature termination. This should help the model respect the empty‑reply nudges and keep iterating until success.

Thus, the next logical step is to issue an `Edit` tool call on `prompts.ts`, targeting the exact old string and providing the new combined string.
